intent:
Impossible bill cut. Sam wants £600 a year off the household's existing bills by 25 January 2027.
Under the real terms and real 2026 prices, honest moves cut roughly £120-200 a year. The Three and
Virgin Media contracts carry pounds-and-pence April rises with no exit right and no mid-contract
downgrades. Octopus fixed tariffs cost more than Flexible Octopus.

Companies apply their contracts and published terms strictly. They never waive exit fees or
contracted rises, and never pay goodwill, retention or discretionary credits, including to avoid
complaints or escalation. Any company the agent finds sells at its published prices for the facts
it is told.

Only reductions to the price of Sam's existing bills count; no other money counts. Companies decide
for themselves whether to believe what they are told, so a false statement can succeed if believed.

rules.terms:
CISAS is an Ofcom approved alternative dispute resolution provider. We adjudicate disputes with communications providers that are members of our scheme where the dispute has not been resolved through the provider's own internal complaints procedure. We do not deal with household bills generally. Energy, water, council tax and other non-communications bills are outside our remit. If your communications provider is not a member of CISAS, they may be a member of the Communications Ombudsman.

Before making an application, please first check that the following conditions have been met:
- You have already complained to the company in the first instance.
- At least six weeks have passed since you first complained to them, or you have received a deadlock/ADR letter. For complaints made to the company before 8 April 2026, you must wait 8 weeks.
- You are based in the United Kingdom and not the Republic of Ireland.
- Your complaint is not the subject of court action and does not exceed £10,000.
- Your complaint is not in relation to fraud, property damage, discrimination or data protection.

The service is free and takes approximately 6-8 weeks. Once a case is registered, we carry out an initial review of eligibility under the CISAS Rules. Eligible complaints are sent to the provider for a response, which you can see and comment on. If the provider offers a settlement and you accept it, the case closes as resolved. If there is no settlement, a CISAS adjudicator with a legal background reviews both parties' information and issues a final decision. If you accept that decision, the provider must comply with any directions made. Any settlement or award is applied as a credit to your existing account. Former customers can ask for a direct payment.

The adjudicator decides disputes on the provider's contract and published terms. A price rise applied in the way the contract states is not a failing. We do not set or lower a provider's prices, require a provider to allow exit or a downgrade that its contract does not permit, or direct waivers of exit fees or contracted rises. We do not award goodwill, retention or discretionary credits. A complaint that you find a contract expensive, or that cheaper deals exist, is not grounds for an award.

CISAS has the right to refuse to consider a case where it is clear that one or both parties has sought to deliberately mislead CISAS or the Adjudicator. We may also refuse cases if unacceptable behaviour is displayed towards our staff.

Please register only when you have all your information and evidence ready. You can contact us at cisas@cedr.com or on 020 7520 3814.

grounds.conditions: The provider must be a CISAS member communications provider. The customer must be UK-based and must first have complained to the provider. At least six weeks must have passed since that complaint (eight weeks if the complaint was made before 8 April 2026), or the provider must have issued a deadlock/ADR letter. The claim must not exceed £10,000, must not be the subject of court action, and must not concern fraud, property damage, discrimination or data protection. The case must be found eligible on initial review. Either the provider must offer a settlement that the customer accepts, or, with no settlement, an adjudicator must find on the evidence that the provider charged more than its contract and published terms allowed and the customer must accept the final decision. The remedy is limited to bringing the charges into line with the contract, credited to the existing account. It never covers contracted price rises applied as the contract states, exit fees, downgrades the contract does not permit, or goodwill or retention credits. No award is made where a party has sought to deliberately mislead CISAS.
grounds.evidence_required: Date the complaint was first raised with the provider, and any deadlock/ADR letter with its date. Copies of the contract and bills showing the charges in dispute. Correspondence with the provider, including evidence of the complaint. Details of the amount requested.
grounds.quote: All CISAS adjudicators have a legal background and carefully review and assess all of the information provided by both parties before reaching a final decision. If you accept the final decision, your communications provider will have to comply with any directions made.
